paragraphs: Celldex Therapeutics, Inc., which we refer to as "Celldex," "we," "us," "our" or the "Company," is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to exploring the science of mast cell biology and developing therapeutic antibodies which have the ability to engage the human immune system and/or directly affect critical pathways to improve the lives of patients with severe inflammatory, allergic, autoimmune and other devastating diseases. Our drug candidates include monoclonal and bispecific antibodies designed to address mast cell mediated diseases for which available treatments are inadequate.
We are focusing our efforts and resources on the continued research and development of

● Barzolvolimab (also referred to as CDX-0159), a monoclonal antibody that specifically binds the KIT receptor and potently inhibits its activity, which is currently being studied across multiple mast cell driven diseases including

- Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (CSU): In February 2026, we announced that enrollment is complete in our Phase 3 studies in CSU and that topline data will be available in the fourth quarter of 2026. In November 2023, we announced that our Phase 2 study in CSU achieved the primary efficacy endpoint (statistically significant mean change from baseline to Week 12 of urticaria activity score compared to placebo) and was well tolerated. Patients on study continued to receive barzolvolimab and, in September 2024, we reported data from 52 weeks of treatment—demonstrating sustained and deepening disease efficacy and a well tolerated long term safety profile. In June 2025, Celldex presented longer term follow up data from the study. At 76 weeks, 7 months after the completion of dosing with barzolvolimab, over 40% of patients (150 mg Q4W) continued to experience profound, sustained complete response and improved quality of life;

- Cold Urticaria (ColdU) and Symptomatic Dermographism (SD): We initiated a Phase 3 study in ColdU and SD in December 2025 and enrollment is ongoing. In July 2024, we announced that our Phase 2 study being conducted in two forms of chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU), ColdU and SD, achieved the primary efficacy endpoint (statistically significant difference between the percent of patients with a negative provocation test compared to placebo at Week 12) and was well tolerated. 12 week data from the CIndU study were presented in October of 2024 and all secondary endpoints across the study were also met and were highly statistically significant and clinically meaningful. Patients on study continued to receive barzolvolimab and, in November 2025, we reported data from 20 weeks of treatment—demonstrating sustained efficacy and a well tolerated safety profile over the longer treatment period;

- Prurigo Nodularis (PN): In April 2024, we initiated a Phase 2 study in PN and enrollment was completed in December 2025. Topline data from the study is expected in summer 2026. Positive data from a Phase 1b study in PN was reported in November 2023; and
- Atopic Dermatitis (AD): A Phase 2 study in AD was initiated in December 2024 and enrollment was completed in January 2026. Topline data from the study is expected in late 2026.

● Our next generation bispecific antibody platform to support pipeline expansion with additional candidates for inflammatory diseases. Targets are being selected based on new science as well as their compatibility to be used in bispecific antibody formats with our existing antibody programs. Development is focused on emerging, important pathways controlling inflammatory diseases.

- CDX-622 (TSLP & SCF): Our first bispecific candidate for inflammatory diseases is CDX-622 which targets two complementary pathways that drive chronic inflammation, potently neutralizing the alarmin thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) and depleting mast cells via stem cell factor (SCF) starvation. In November 2024, a Phase 1a dose-escalation study in healthy volunteers was initiated and enrollment was completed in January 2026. Positive data from the single ascending dose portion of the study was presented in October 2025. Data from the multiple ascending dose portion of the study and subcutaneous administration are anticipated in the third quarter of 2026. In January 2026, we initiated an open-label, single-dose Phase 1 proof of mechanism study in adults with mild to moderate asthma.
More detail on these programs is provided in the Clinical Development Programs section.

Our mission is to build a fully integrated, commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company that develops important therapies for patients with unmet medical needs. We believe our program assets provide us with the strategic options to either retain full economic rights to our innovative therapies or seek favorable economic terms through advantageous commercial partnerships. This approach allows us to maximize the overall value of our technology and product portfolio while best ensuring the expeditious development of each individual product.

Our future success depends upon many factors, including our ability, and that of any licensees and collaborators that we may have, to successfully develop, obtain regulatory approval for and commercialize our drug candidates. We have had no commercial revenues from sales of our drug candidates, and we have had a history of operating losses. It is possible that we may not be able to successfully develop, obtain regulatory approval for, or commercialize, our drug candidates, and we are subject to a number of risks that you should be aware of before investing in us. These risks are described more fully in "Item 1A. Risk Factors."

Barzolvolimab is a humanized monoclonal antibody that specifically binds the receptor tyrosine kinase KIT and potently inhibits its activity. KIT is expressed in a variety of cells, including mast cells, and its activation by its ligand SCF regulates mast cell growth, differentiation, survival, chemotaxis and degranulation. Barzolvolimab is designed to block KIT activation by disrupting both SCF binding and KIT dimerization. By targeting KIT, barzolvolimab has been shown to inhibit mast cell activity and decrease mast cell numbers, which we believe could provide potential clinical benefit in mast cell related diseases.

Barzolvolimab was initially studied in chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU), diseases where mast cell degranulation plays a central role in the onset and progression of the disease. In July 2024, we initiated two Phase 3 studies in CSU. In February 2026, we announced that enrollment is complete in the Phase 3 studies and that topline data is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. In November 2023, we reported that barzolvolimab achieved the primary efficacy endpoint in a Phase 2 study in CSU, with a statistically significant mean change from baseline to Week 12 of UAS7 (weekly urticaria activity score) compared to placebo and was well tolerated. In September 2024, we presented 52 week treatment data from the CSU study, demonstrating sustained and deepening disease efficacy and a well tolerated long term safety profile. In June 2025, we presented follow up data from this study through Week 76, 7 months after the completion of dosing with barzolvolimab, demonstrating ongoing profound, sustained complete response and improved quality of life. The study is complete. In April 2024, we announced enrollment was complete in the ongoing Phase 2 CIndU study. In July 2024, we announced that our Phase 2 study in CIndU achieved the primary efficacy endpoint, (statistically significant difference between the percent of patients with a negative provocation test compared to placebo at Week 12) and was well tolerated. 12 week data from the CIndU study were presented in October of 2024 and all secondary endpoints across the study were also met and were highly statistically significant and clinically meaningful. Patients on study continued to receive barzolvolimab for 20 weeks of treatment and were then followed for up to 24 additional weeks without treatment. In November 2025, data from the 20 week placebo controlled treatment period were presented, demonstrating sustained efficacy and a favorable safety profile. Patients with returning or continuing symptoms were eligible to enroll into an open label extension (OLE). The study is now complete.

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Condition and Capital Requirements
Risks Related to Development and Regulatory Approval of Drug Candidates
Risks Related to Commercialization of Our Drug Candidates
Risks Related to Reliance on Third Parties
Risks Related to Our Capital Stock
We currently have no product revenue and will need to raise capital to operate our business.
We expect to incur future losses and we may never become profitable.
Our long-term success depends heavily on our ability to fund and complete the research and development activities and obtain regulatory approval for our program assets.
Our drug candidates are subject to extensive regulatory scrutiny.
If our drug candidates do not pass required tests for safety and effectiveness, we will not be able to obtain regulatory approval and derive commercial revenue from them.
Product testing is critical to the success of our drug candidates but subject to delay or cancellation if we have difficulty enrolling patients.
We may have delays in commencing, enrolling and completing our clinical trials, and we may not complete them at all.
We may be unable to manage multiple late-stage clinical trials for a variety of drug candidates simultaneously.

Failure to successfully validate, develop and obtain regulatory approval for companion diagnostics for our drug candidates, if needed, could harm our drug development strategy and operational results.
Any delay in obtaining regulatory approval would have an adverse impact on our ability to earn future revenues.

If our drug candidates for which we obtain regulatory approval do not achieve broad acceptance from physicians, patients and third-party payors, we may be unable to generate significant revenues, if any.
Other factors could affect the demand for and sales and profitability of any drug candidates that we may commercialize in the future.
Failure to obtain regulatory approvals in foreign jurisdictions will prevent us from marketing our products internationally.
If we obtain approval to commercialize any approved products outside of the United States, a variety of risks associated with international operations could materially adversely affect our business.
paragraphs: You should consider carefully these risk factors together with all of the information included or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report in addition to our financial statements and the notes to our financial statements. This section includes forward-looking statements.

The following is a discussion of the risk factors that we believe are material to us at this time. These risks and uncertainties are not the only ones facing us, and there may be additional matters that we are unaware of or that we currently consider immaterial. All of these could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
● Risks related to our need for additional capital to fund our operations.
● Risks related to the Merger Agreement and related Settlement Agreement with Kolltan.
● Risks related to our ability to fund and complete the research and development activities and obtain regulatory approval for our program assets.
● Risks related to the extensive and lengthy regulatory scrutiny to which we are subject.

paragraphs: Celldex Therapeutics, Inc., 哪些我們稱為 "Celldex," "we," "us," "our" 或 the "Company," 是一家生技製藥公司，專注於探索 mast cell 生物學的科學，並開發具備能力與人類免疫系統互動及/或直接影響關鍵路徑，以改善患有嚴重發炎、過敏、自身免疫及其他致命疾病的病患生活品質的治療性單株抗體。我們的藥物候選品包括單株及雙特異性抗體，設計用以針對 mast cell 所引發的疾病，而現有治療方式不足。
我們正將努力與資源集中在持續研究與開發
● Barzolvolimab (也稱為 CDX-0159)，一種單株抗體，專門與 KIT 受體結合，並強效抑制其活性，目前正被研究用於多種 mast cell 所驅動的疾病，包括

- 慢性自發性蕁麻疹 (CSU)：2026 年 2 月，我們宣佈在 CSU 的 Phase 3 研究中，招募已經完成，且初步數據預計於 2026 年第四季公佈。2023 年 11 月，我們宣佈在 CSU 的 Phase 2 研究中，達成主要療效終點（與安慰劑相比，基線至第 12 週的蕁麻疹活動評分有統計顯著的平均變化），且耐受性良好。參與研究的病患持續接受 barzolvolimab 治療，2024 年 9 月，我們報告了 52 週的治療數據—顯示持續且深化的疾病療效，以及良好的長期安全性。2025 年 6 月，Celldex 展示了該研究的長期追蹤數據。在 76 週，也就是 barzolvolimab 給藥完成後 7 個月，超過 40% 的病患（150 mg Q4W）持續經歷顯著、持續的完全反應，並改善生活品質；

- 冷症蕁麻疹 (ColdU) 和症狀性皮膚劃痕症 (SD)：我們於 2025 年 12 月啟動了 ColdU 和 SD 的 Phase 3 研究，招募持續進行中。2024 年 7 月，我們宣佈在兩種慢性誘發性蕁麻疹 (CIndU) 的 Phase 2 研究中，ColdU 和 SD，達成主要療效終點（與安慰劑相比，第 12 週的負誘發測試患者百分比有統計顯著的差異），且耐受性良好。2024 年 10 月，我們展示了 CIndU 研究的 12 週數據，且該研究的所有次要終點也都達成，且具有高度統計顯著性與臨牀意義。參與研究的病患持續接受 barzolvolimab 治療，2025 年 11 月，我們報告了 20 週的治療數據—顯示在較長治療期間持續的療效，以及良好的安全性；
- 瘙癢性結節性皮膚炎 (PN)：我們於 2024 年 4 月啟動了 PN 的 Phase 2 研究，招募於 2025 年 12 月完成。該研究的初步數據預計於 2026 年夏天公佈。2023 年 11 月，我們報告了 PN 的 Phase 1b 研究的正面數據；且
- 動態皮膚炎 (AD)：AD 的 Phase 2 研究於 2024 年 12 月啟動，招募於 2026 年 1 月完成。該研究的初步數據預計於 2026 年年底公佈。
● 我們的下一代雙特異性抗體平台，用以支持管線擴張，並加入更多針對發炎疾病的候選品。目標是根據新科學以及與現有抗體計畫相容性，選擇適合用於雙特異性抗體格式的目標。開發重點為控制發炎疾病的新興、重要的路徑。

- CDX-622 (TSLP & SCF)：本公司第一個用於炎症疾病的雙特異性候選藥物為 CDX-622，其針對兩種驅動慢性炎症的補充途徑，強效中和警報分子胸腺間質淋巴細胞生成素（TSLP），並透過幹細胞因子（SCF）飢餓化來減少肥大細胞。2024 年 11 月，本公司啟動了一項針對健康志願者的第一期 A 相關劑量遞增研究，並於 2026 年 1 月完成入組。該研究單劑量遞增部分的正面數據於 2025 年 10 月發表。該研究多劑量遞增部分及皮下給藥數據預計於 2026 年第三季發表。2026 年 1 月，本公司啟動了一項開放標籤、單劑量的第一期 A 作用機制研究，用於輕度至中度氣喘成人患者。
這些計畫的更多細節請參閱「臨牀開發計畫」部分。
本公司使命為建立一家完整整合、商業化階段的生物製藥公司，開發對未滿足醫療需求的患者重要的治療方案。本公司相信我們的計畫資產使我們擁有戰略選擇，可以保留創新治療的完整經濟權利，或透過有利的商業合作夥伴關係尋求有利的經濟條件。此方法使我們能最大化我們的技術與產品組合的總體價值，同時確保每個個別產品的快速開發。
本公司未來的成功取決於許多因素，包括本公司及其任何授權人與合作夥伴能否成功開發、取得監管批准並商業化我們的藥物候選品。我們尚未從銷售我們的藥物候選品中獲得任何商業收入，且我們有經營虧損的歷史。我們可能無法成功開發、取得監管批准或商業化我們的藥物候選品，且我們面臨許多風險，投資人投資前應知悉這些風險。這些風險在「項目 1A. 風險因素」中更詳細說明。

Barzolvolimab 是一種人類化單株抗體，專門與受體酪胺酸 kinase KIT 結合，並強效抑制其活性。KIT 表達於多種細胞中，包括肥大細胞，其被其配體 SCF 激活，調控肥大細胞的增殖、分化、存活、趨化及脫顆粒。Barzolvolimab 設計用來透過幹擾 SCF 結合及 KIT 細胞聚體化來阻斷 KIT 激活。透過針對 KIT，Barzolvolimab 已顯示能抑制肥大細胞活性並減少肥大細胞數量，我們相信這可能為肥大細胞相關疾病提供潛在的臨牀效益。

Barzolvolimab 最初在慢性自發性風疹（CSU）及慢性誘發性風疹（CIndU）中進行研究，這些疾病中肥大細胞脫顆粒在疾病發作及進展中扮演中心角色。2024 年 7 月，本公司啟動了兩項 CSU 的第三期研究。2026 年 2 月，本公司宣佈第三期研究已完成入組，並預期於 2026 年第四季公佈主要數據。2023 年 11 月，本公司報告指出 Barzolvolimab 在 CSU 的第二期研究中達成主要療效終點，與安慰劑相比，週ly 風疹活動指數（UAS7）從基線至第 12 週的統計顯著變化，且耐受性良好。2024 年 9 月，本公司展示 CSU 研究的 52 週治療數據，顯示持續且加深的疾病療效及良好的長期安全性。2025 年 6 月，本公司展示此研究的追蹤數據至第 76 週，即 Barzolvolimab 給藥完成後 7 個月，顯示持續且顯著的完全反應及改善的生活品質。該研究已結束。2024 年 4 月，本公司宣佈持續進行的第二期 CIndU 研究已完成入組。2024 年 7 月，本公司宣佈 CIndU 的第二期研究達成主要療效終點（與安慰劑相比，第 12 週患者負面誘發測試百分比的統計顯著差異），且耐受性良好。2024 年 10 月，本公司展示 CIndU 研究的 12 週數據，並達成所有次要終點，且統計顯著且臨牀意義重大。參與研究的患者持續接受 Barzolvolimab 給藥 20 週，之後再追蹤至最多 24 週無治療期。2025 年 11 月，本公司展示 20 週安慰劑控制治療期的數據，顯示持續療效及良好的安全性。有回歸或持續症狀的患者可加入開放標籤延長研究（OLE）。該研究現已結束。

- 慢性自發性蕁麻疹（CSU）：2026 年 2 月，本公司宣佈已完成 CSU 的第三期臨牀試驗入組，並預計於 2026 年第四季公佈初步數據。2023 年 11 月，本公司宣佈在 CSU 的第二期臨牀試驗中達成主要療效終點（與安慰劑相比，基線至第 12 週的蕁麻疹活動評分有統計顯著的平均變化），且耐受性良好。參與試驗的病患持續接受 Barzolvolimab 治療，2024 年 9 月，本公司報告了 52 週治療的數據—顯示療效持續且加深，且長期安全性良好。2025 年 6 月，Celldex 展示了試驗的長期追蹤數據。在 76 週，即 Barzolvolimab 給藥完成後 7 個月，超過 40% 的病患（150 mg Q4W）持續經驗到顯著且持續的完全反應，並改善生活品質；

- 冷性蕁麻疹（ColdU）及症狀性 Dermographism（SD）：本公司於 2025 年 12 月啟動了 ColdU 和 SD 的第三期臨牀試驗，目前入組仍在進行中。2024 年 7 月，本公司宣佈在兩種慢性誘發性蕁麻疹（CIndU）形式，即 ColdU 和 SD 的第二期臨牀試驗中達成主要療效終點（與安慰劑相比，第 12 週患者負誘發測試百分比有統計顯著差異），且耐受性良好。2024 年 10 月，本公司展示了 CIndU 試驗的 12 週數據，並達成所有次要終點，且統計顯著且臨牀意義重大。參與試驗的病患持續接受 Barzolvolimab 治療，2025 年 11 月，本公司報告了 20 週治療的數據—顯示療效持續且安全性良好；
- 瘙癢性結節性皮膚炎（PN）：2024 年 4 月，本公司啟動了 PN 的第二期臨牀試驗，並於 2025 年 12 月完成入組。預計於 2026 年夏天公佈試驗的初步數據。2023 年 11 月，本公司報告了 PN 的第一期b試驗的正面數據；且
- 動態皮膚炎（AD）：AD 的第二期臨牀試驗於 2024 年 12 月啟動，並於 2026 年 1 月完成入組。預計於 2026 年年底公佈試驗的初步數據。
● 我們的下一代雙特異性抗體平台，用以支持管線擴張，並加入更多針對發炎疾病的候選品。目標是根據新科學以及與我們現有抗體計畫相容性，選擇適合用於雙特異性抗體格式的目標。開發重點為控制發炎疾病的關鍵新興且重要的路徑。

- CDX-622 (TSLP & SCF): 我們第一個用於發炎疾病的雙特異性候選藥物為 CDX-622，其針對兩種補充性的通路，驅動慢性發炎，強效中和警報分子胸腺星狀細胞淋巴opoietin (TSLP)，並透過幹細胞因子 (SCF) 狀態飢餓來消耗肥大細胞。2024 年 11 月，我們啟動了一項針對健康志工的 Phase 1a 劑量遞增研究，並於 2026 年 1 月完成招募。該研究單劑遞增部分的正面數據於 2025 年 10 月發表。預計 2026 年第三季將公佈該研究多劑遞增部分及皮下給藥的數據。2026 年 1 月，我們啟動了一項開放標籤、單劑 Phase 1 作用機制研究，用於輕度至中度氣喘成人患者。
這些計畫的更多細節請參閱 Clinical Development Programs 節。
我們的使命是建立一家完整整合、商業階段的生物製藥公司，開發對未滿足醫療需求的患者重要的治療方案。我們相信我們的計畫資產使我們擁有戰略選擇，可以保留創新治療的全部經濟權利，或透過有利的經濟條款尋求商業合作夥伴。這種方法使我們能最大化我們的技術與產品組合的總價值，同時確保每個個別產品的快速開發。
執行我們商業計畫所需的支出將面臨許多不確定性。臨牀試驗的完成可能需要數年或更久，且通常根據藥物候選物的類型、複雜性、創新性及預期用途而有很大差異。這些類型的藥物候選物的臨牀開發通常需要五至數年，且每種藥物候選物的總開發成本可能超過數百萬美元。我們估計，我們通常進行的臨牀試驗類型，通常完成的時間如下：

與本公司資本股票相關的風險
本公司目前尚未有產品收入，並將需要籌集資金以運作本公司業務。
本公司預期將產生未來虧損，且可能永遠無法實現盈利。
本公司長期成功嚴重依賴本公司能否籌資並完成研究與開發活動，以及取得我們計畫資產的監管批准。
本公司藥物候選品面臨嚴格的監管審查。
若本公司藥物候選品未能通過安全性和有效性所需的測試，本公司將無法取得監管批准，並從這些藥物中獲得商業收入。
產品測試對本公司藥物候選品的成功至關重要，但若本公司在招募病患方面遇到困難，產品測試可能延宕或取消。
我們可能在啟動、納入受試者及完成臨牀試驗方面遭遇延遲，也可能完全無法完成這些試驗。
我們可能無法同時管理多項晚期臨牀試驗，針對多種藥物候選品。
若未能成功驗證、開發並取得伴診診斷工具的監管批准（如需），可能會損害我們的藥物開發策略及營運結果。
任何取得監管批准的延遲，將對我們未來獲取收入的能力產生不利影響。
若我們取得監管批准的藥物候選品未能獲得醫生、患者及第三方付款方的廣泛接受，我們可能無法產生顯著收入，甚至無收入。
其他因素可能影響我們未來可能商業化的藥物候選品的市場需求及銷售與獲利能力。
若未能取得海外司法管轄區的監管批准，將會阻止我們在國際市場推廣產品。
若我們取得在美國以外地區商業化已批准產品的批准，與國際營運相關的各種風險可能會對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮這些風險因素，並與本年度報告中所包含或參考的資訊，以及我們的財務報表與財務報表附註一併審閱。本節包含前瞻性陳述。
以下為我們認為目前對我們而言屬重要之風險因素。這些風險與不確定性並非我們唯一面臨的風險，且可能尚有其他我們未察覺或目前認為不重要之事項。所有這些都可能對我們的業務、營運成果、財務狀況與現金流產生不利影響。
● 與我們需要額外資金以支應營運之相關風險。
● 與我們與 Kolltan 簽訂之合併協議及相關和解協議相關之風險。
● 與我們能否支應並完成研究與開發活動，並取得我們計畫資產之監管批准相關之風險。
● 與我們所面臨之廣泛且漫長之監管審查相關之風險。
